title: Nüshu, the women's script of Jiangyong
summary: Nüshu is a script developed and used only by women in Jiangyong County, Hunan, China, mainly for letters between sworn sisters, wedding and funeral texts and ballads. Its origins are debated: one scholar places its development between the late Ming and the Qing, while UNESCO's Courier dates it to the nineteenth century, with a coin of 1851-1864 as the earliest known artefact.

uncertainty.note: Tate Papers: development between the late Ming (1550-1644) and Qing (1644-1912) dynasties. UNESCO Courier: origin in the nineteenth century, earliest artefact a coin of 1851-1864. Start 1550 is the earliest bound given; the id year 1800 is only a lookup key.
